name: hackage-haskell
description: Hackage, the Haskell community's package archive: search packages, read package metadata, versions, dependencies, reverse dependencies, changelogs, documentation indexes, tags, categories, recent uploads, deprecated and candidate packages, and maintainer profiles.

commands.name: search-packages
commands.summary: Search Hackage packages by keyword, with optional filter expressions in the query, sorting and pagination (50 results per page)

params.name: query
params.description: Search words, optionally followed by filter expressions in parentheses. Examples: (tag:json), (downloads > 10), (maintainer:SimonMarlow), (not tag:network), (lastUpload < 2021-10-29)

params.name: page
params.description: Zero-based page number. Each page has 50 results.

commands.name: get-package
commands.summary: Get a package's detail page: synopsis, description, latest version, modules and changelog link

params.name: package
params.description: Package name, optionally with a version (e.g. parsec or parsec-3.1.18.0)

commands.name: get-package-versions
commands.summary: List all versions of a package with their status (normal or deprecated), as JSON

commands.name: get-preferred-versions
commands.summary: Get a package's preferred versions (normal-version list, plus deprecated versions if any), as JSON

commands.name: get-package-dependencies
commands.summary: List the dependencies and version constraints of a specific package version

params.name: package_version
params.description: Package name with version, e.g. parsec3-1.0.1.8

commands.name: list-reverse-dependencies
commands.summary: List the packages that depend on a given package (reverse dependencies of its latest version)

commands.name: get-changelog
commands.summary: Get the changelog of a specific package version

params.name: package_version
params.description: Package name with version, e.g. parsec-3.1.18.0

commands.name: get-docs-index
commands.summary: Get the Haddock identifier index (functions, types and their modules) for a package version, as JSON

params.name: package_version
params.description: Package name with version, e.g. commonmark-extensions-0.2.7.3

commands.name: list-recent-uploads
commands.summary: List the 20 most recently uploaded package versions on Hackage, newest first, from the recent-uploads RSS feed. Each item has the package-version title, package link, upload date, and a description na

commands.name: list-packages-by-tag
commands.summary: List all packages that have a given tag (e.g. parsing, json, network)

params.name: tag
params.description: Tag name, e.g. parsing, json, bsd3

commands.name: list-categories
commands.summary: List all package categories with their package counts

commands.name: list-deprecated-packages
commands.summary: List deprecated packages and the packages that replace them

commands.name: list-candidates
commands.summary: List candidate package versions (uploaded for review but not yet published)

commands.name: get-user
commands.summary: Get a Hackage user's profile: the package groups (maintainers, candidates) they belong to

notes: search-packages: the page number starts at 0. list-recent-uploads: the page number starts at 1.

Search filters go inside the query string as parenthesized expressions, e.g. 'json parser (tag:json) (downloads > 10)'. Deprecated packages are hidden unless the query includes (deprecated:any) or (deprecated:true).

The values name.uri and maintainers[].uri in search results are site paths. Strip the '/package/' prefix to get the argument for get-package or get-package-versions, and the '/user/' prefix to get the argument for get-user.

These commands need a versioned package id (name-version, e.g. parsec-3.1.18.0): get-package-dependencies, get-changelog and get-docs-index. To find the latest version, call get-package-versions or get-preferred-versions.
The working reverse-dependency path is /package/{name}/reverse. /packages/reverse/{name} returns 404.
Some HTML list extractions also match header or menu rows (tr/li). Skip items with empty package or name fields.
Hackage documents its server API at /api. Many resources are also served as JSON, e.g. /package/{name}.json and /user/{name}.
